title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Social Science (087) · Geography: Contemporary India II · Crash revision (2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written from this video's script, its worksheet and the NCERT/CBSE material it cites, modelled on most-repeated / high-weightage question types in CBSE Sample Question Papers and past board papers. Practice for readiness only: not predictions of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 39 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number.

S1.name: Resources and Development
S1.tip: Four ways to classify resources; three steps of resource planning; six soils with their features and crops. Land use: culturable waste > 5 years, current fallow ≤ 1 year. Read status-of-development stems carefully.
S1.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 1 Resources and Development

S2.name: Forest and Wildlife Resources
S2.tip: Dates: 1972 Wildlife Act, 1973 Project Tiger, 1988 Joint Forest Management (Odisha first). Tiger reserves with states. Community movements: Chipko, Beej Bachao (Tehri), Navdanya, Bhairodev Dakav Sonchuri (Alwar), Bishnois.
S2.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 2 Forest and Wildlife Resources

S3.name: Water Resources
S3.tip: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej-Beas), Hirakud (Mahanadi), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada). Match each rainwater-harvesting method to its region: guls/kuls (W Himalayas), khadins/johads (Rajasthan), tankas (Bikaner, Phalodi, Barmer), bamboo drip (Meghalaya).
S3.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 3 Water Resources

S4.name: Agriculture
S4.tip: Learn crop conditions as numbers: rice > 25°C, > 100 cm; wheat 50–75 cm, cool growing season; sugarcane 21–27°C, 75–100 cm; rubber > 25°C, > 200 cm; cotton 210 frost-free days. Rabi Oct–Dec, kharif with monsoon, zaid in summer.
S4.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 4 Agriculture

S5.name: Minerals and Energy Resources
S5.tip: Mode of occurrence (veins, beds, residual, placer); four iron-ore belts; bauxite Odisha; mica Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh; Gondwana coal in the Damodar valley; oil at Mumbai High, Ankleshwar, Digboi. Practise 3 + 2 'role + distribution' answers.
S5.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 5 Minerals and Energy Resources

S6.name: Manufacturing Industries
S6.tip: Importance of manufacturing (jobs, modern agriculture, exports, less regional disparity); classification by raw material, role, ownership, bulk; steel inputs 4 : 2 : 1; three-stage effluent treatment; pollution controls.
S6.ncert: NCERT Contemporary India II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 6 Manufacturing Industries

S7.name: Geography Map Work
S7.tip: Learn the CBSE map list with a clue for each: dams, mines, thermal and nuclear plants, cotton and steel centres, software technology parks, 10 major ports, 6 international airports.
S7.ncert: CBSE Social Science Curriculum 2026-27 Geography map list; SQP 2026-27 Q19; NCERT Ch 7 Lifelines (map only)

questions.question: Agenda 21 was adopted at:
questions.explanation: The Rio Earth Summit of June 1992 adopted Agenda 21 for sustainable development.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Resources and Development; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit, 1992

questions.question: A soil holds moisture well, is rich in lime and potash but poor in phosphorus, and is ideal for cotton. It is:
questions.explanation: Black soil of the Deccan trap region: moisture-retentive, cotton soil.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Resources and Development; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: About 43% of India's land area is plains and 30% is mountains. What percentage is plateau?
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Resources and Development; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Land that has been left uncultivated for more than five agricultural years is called:
questions.explanation: Culturable waste: uncultivated for more than 5 agricultural years; current fallow: 1 year or less.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Resources and Development; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In which group of states is over-irrigation the main cause of land degradation?
questions.explanation: Over-irrigation → waterlogging and salinity in Punjab, Haryana, western UP; mining causes degradation in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, MP, Odisha; overgrazing in Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Resources and Development; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh

questions.question: Project Tiger was launched in:
questions.explanation: 1972: Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act; 1973: Project Tiger (tigers had fallen to 1,827).
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Forest and Wildlife Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which tiger reserve is correctly matched with its state?
questions.explanation: Corbett–Uttarakhand, Sunderbans–West Bengal, Bandhavgarh–MP, Sariska–Rajasthan, Manas–Assam, Periyar–Kerala.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Forest and Wildlife Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which state has the largest area under permanent forests?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh: permanent forests make up 75% of its forest area.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Forest and Wildlife Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Joint Forest Management, begun in Odisha in 1988, involves:
questions.explanation: Communities manage and restore degraded forest land and get a share of the forest produce.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Forest and Wildlife Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Local villages protecting degraded forests and sharing the benefits
Banning all people from forest areas

questions.question: Five villages in Alwar district declared 1,200 hectares of forest as the Bhairodev Dakav 'Sonchuri', with their own rules. This shows:
questions.explanation: A community-declared sanctuary that bans hunting and protects wildlife against outside encroachment.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Forest and Wildlife Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Forests should be converted to farmland
Only the government can conserve forests
Communities can protect habitats on their own initiative

questions.question: The Bhakra Nangal project in the Sutlej-Beas basin is used mainly for:
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal: hydel power + irrigation; Hirakud (Mahanadi): conservation + flood control.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In which places are 'tankas' (underground tanks) used to store rainwater for drinking?
questions.explanation: Tankas in the dry Thar region; guls/kuls in the western Himalayas; bamboo drip irrigation in Meghalaya.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Bikaner, Phalodi and Barmer in Rajasthan

questions.question: Which was the first state to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all houses?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu made rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all houses across the state.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; the problems in R are the reasons for the criticism in A (also induced earthquakes and salinisation).
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Large multi-purpose dams have come under great criticism in recent years.
questions.reason: They fragment rivers, reduce sediment flow and displace local communities.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: A dry village in western Rajasthan has very little rain and no perennial river. Which traditional method would you suggest for drinking water?
questions.explanation: Tankas suit the arid region; guls/kuls need mountain streams; bamboo drip suits Meghalaya's slopes and springs.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Tankas: underground tanks filled by rooftop rainwater
Guls and kuls (diversion channels from mountain streams)
Bamboo drip irrigation from hill springs

questions.question: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada in Gujarat benefits Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat and Rajasthan.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Water Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which of these is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Rabi (sown Oct–Dec, harvested Apr–Jun): wheat, barley, peas, gram, mustard. Paddy, maize and cotton are kharif.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which conditions suit rice?
questions.explanation: Rice: > 25°C, high humidity, > 100 cm. The other options describe wheat, sugarcane and cotton.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Temperature above 25°C, high humidity and over 100 cm of rain
A cool growing season and 50–75 cm of rain

questions.question: How many frost-free days does cotton need to grow well?
questions.explanation: Cotton: black soil of the Deccan, high temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, 210 frost-free days and bright sunshine.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which statement about rice is correct?
questions.explanation: The same crop can be commercial in one region and subsistence in another.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It is a subsistence crop everywhere in India
It is a commercial crop in Punjab and Haryana but a subsistence crop in Odisha
It is grown only in the zaid season
It needs less than 50 cm of rain

questions.question: A region is hot and humid, with temperatures above 25°C and over 200 cm of rain. Which plantation crop suits it?
questions.explanation: Rubber: > 25°C, > 200 cm (Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andaman and Nicobar, Garo hills).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A farmer's region gets about 60 cm of rain, has a cool growing season and bright sunshine at the time of ripening. Which crop is best?
questions.explanation: Wheat: 50–75 cm of rain, cool growing season, bright sunshine at ripening. Rice, rubber and jute need much more water.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Agriculture; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Gold, silver, tin and platinum found in the sands of valley floors are:
questions.explanation: Placer deposits: minerals in valley sands that are not corroded by water.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which is the finest iron ore, with up to 70% iron?
questions.explanation: Magnetite has up to 70% iron; hematite is the most widely used.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which state leads in bauxite, with deposits at Panchpatmali in Koraput?
questions.explanation: Odisha leads in bauxite (Panchpatmali, Koraput district).
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Gondwana coal fields at Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro lie in the:
questions.explanation: Gondwana coal: Damodar valley; tertiary coal: the north-east; lignite: Neyveli.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Bailadila, whose iron ore has the best physical properties needed for steel, belongs to which belt?
questions.explanation: Bailadila is in the Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt (Chhattisgarh–Maharashtra).
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: About 10 kg of manganese is needed to make one tonne of steel. How many kg of manganese are needed for 5 tonnes of steel?
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which is the oldest oil-producing state of India?
questions.explanation: Assam (Digboi, Naharkatiya); Mumbai High and Ankleshwar (Gujarat) are other fields.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Minerals and Energy Resources; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Where was India's first successful textile mill set up, in 1854?
questions.explanation: 1854: first textile mill, Mumbai; 1855: first jute mill at Rishra near Kolkata.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Manufacturing Industries; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Steel making uses iron ore, coking coal and limestone in the ratio 4 : 2 : 1. If 8 tonnes of iron ore are used, how many tonnes of limestone are needed?
questions.explanation: 4 parts = 8 t, so 1 part = 2 t of limestone (and 4 t of coking coal).
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Manufacturing Industries; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false (Bengaluru is inland). The SQP 2026-27 assertion-reason uses this trap.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Manufacturing Industries; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Bengaluru has emerged as the electronic capital of India.
questions.reason: Bengaluru has a major sea port.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: India spins world-class yarn, yet much of its woven fabric is of lower quality. Why?
questions.explanation: Spinning is centralised and modern, but weaving (handloom, powerloom) is scattered and low-tech.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Manufacturing Industries; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Fabric is woven only in Bengaluru
Weaving is largely decentralised and cannot use much of the high-quality yarn

questions.question: Industrial effluents are treated in three stages. Which order is correct?
questions.explanation: Primary: screening, grinding, settling; secondary: biological; tertiary: biological, chemical and physical recycling.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Manufacturing Industries; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which nuclear power plant on the CBSE map list is in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Tarapur (Maharashtra); Kakrapara (Gujarat); Narora (UP); Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu).
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Geography Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which international airport on the map list is in Punjab?
questions.explanation: The six airports: Amritsar, Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai (Meenambakkam), Kolkata, Hyderabad.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Geography Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: The Salal dam on the CBSE map list is on the river:
questions.explanation: Salal on the Chenab; Bhakra Nangal on the Sutlej; Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada; Hirakud on the Mahanadi.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Geography Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which iron and steel plant on the map list is in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagar (Karnataka), Salem (Tamil Nadu), Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Durgapur (West Bengal).
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Geography Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which major sea port is correctly matched with its state?
questions.explanation: Paradip–Odisha, Kandla–Gujarat, Tuticorin–Tamil Nadu, Haldia–West Bengal.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: Geography Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.
